title: Admin activity stream: normalized exports with per-field redaction & async export UI
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Admin teams need reliable, privacy-safe exports of console activity for compliance and incident investigations. Current export paths mix formats, expose columns that require manual redaction, and block for large result sets. Goal: provide normalized CSV and NDJSON export outputs with per-field redaction policies (driven by RBAC v2), an async export job UI for large result sets, and consistent timestamps/IDs that make exported artifacts easy to correlate with SSO/SAML session records. Non-goal: building a full forensic analysis UX or changing retention schedules.
acceptance_criteria: UI: Admins can run a filtered search in the Audit Console and trigger an export job that returns a downloadable artifact (CSV or NDJSON) via the async job list

Redaction: Fields marked as PII by policy (email, ip_address, api_key, session_token) are redacted in exports according to RBAC v2 rules for the requesting user; redaction must be deterministic and documented
Format normalization: CSV exports use a canonical column order and ISO-8601 UTC timestamps; NDJSON exports include a manifest file describing schema and redaction policy applied
Performance: Exports up to 10M rows are accepted as async jobs; small exports (<50k rows) are fast-path streamed with progress shown in the UI
Auditability: Each export job records the requester, filters used, RBAC role snapshot, and a pointer to the stored artifact; these are themselves stored in audit logs
Security: Export artifacts stored temporarily in object storage are encrypted and access-controlled; URLs expire and are scoped to the requesting org/team
Tests: E2E tests validate redaction permutations across RBAC roles, and integration tests confirm exported timestamps correlate to SSO session IDs
tasks: Design: final UI mockups for async export modal and job list (link in artifacts)
API: add /audit/exports POST endpoint to enqueue export jobs (format, filters, max_rows, include_manifest)
Worker: implement worker to materialize export; apply per-field redaction via RBAC v2 policy snapshot
Storage: use signed, encrypted object keys; implement lifecycle to delete after 30 days by default
Console: implement quick-path stream for small exports using chunked transfer with progress events
RBAC: integrate with RBAC v2 snapshotting to capture permission state at time of export
Telemetry: emit metrics (export_requested, export_completed, rows_exported, redaction_rate, export_failure_reason)
Docs: update Admin Audit Export doc with examples for CSV/NDJSON and manifest format
QA: build e2e matrix for role permutations (admin, security-analyst, read-only) and redaction permutations
decisions: Use async export jobs for >50k rows to avoid blocking request paths and to allow retries/observability
Support two artifact formats: CSV for analysts, NDJSON with schema manifest for downstream processing
Apply redaction deterministically (replace with <redacted:type>) so that downstream tooling can detect fields that were redacted
Snapshot RBAC v2 role set at job creation to ensure exports are reproducible and auditable, even if roles change later
Encrypt artifacts at rest in S3-compatible storage and ensure presigned URLs are scoped to the requesting org
tradeoffs: Async jobs add complexity (queue/operator surface) but are necessary for reliably handling large exports without degrading console responsiveness
Deterministic redaction disallows returning masked partial data (e.g., last 4 chars of tokens) to simplify policy enforcement; may require future opt-in for masked reveal
Manifest increases artifact size but significantly reduces ambiguity for downstream consumers and helps with automated ingestion
